chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Udaym ibn al-Ḥurr, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام instructed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding all the prayers, and he assigned for every prayer two times, except al-maghrib, for indeed he assigned for it one time only.

key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, the angel who conveyed divine instruction
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.وَقْتَيْنِ: two designated times for a prayer

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the time of maghrib prayer compared to the other daily prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام taught the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم the prescribed times of the daily prayers. It indicates that each prayer has two times except al-maghrib, which is given a single time, making it significant in discussions of prayer timings in fiqh.
